stem: A pharmacist directly oversees sterile and complex nonsterile compounding. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: The applicable sterile-compounding CE requirement must be met annually.
General pharmacy-law CE automatically replaces all compounding CE.
The applicable complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement must also be assessed.
Compounding CE applies only to technicians.
Current USP chapters eliminate state CE requirements.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.

choice_analysis.A: The proposition 'The applicable sterile-compounding CE requirement must be met annually.' is supported by Massachusetts compounding continuing education: A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.
choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'The applicable complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement must also be assessed.' is supported by Massachusetts compounding continuing education: A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
